origin: Scripted app demo • sample data. Producer-supplied WPF visual-tree frames use unchanged production XAML and app reducers in a private source copy with isolated I/O adapters, sample transcripts and a fake provider. This is not desktop video or a recording of physical OS mouse input. Cursor guides illustrate scripted control activation; keyboard badges show supplied handler inputs. Narration is synthetic Windows System.Speech TTS. Recording states and provider responses are samples: no real audio or inference. Native installation, file-picker and provider setup steps are instructional boundaries, not evidence that those operations were executed.
caveat: This tutorial shows the current local source. Previous-answer context is not included in the published v0.2.0-preview.1 installer. The published installer is an unsigned Windows 11 x64 preview, not universal capture qualification.

cues.text: Welcome to the complete Phantom Fudge tutorial.
We will walk through audio, notes, questions, answers, follow-ups,
keyboard controls, and day-to-day recovery.
Use the chapter list beside the video to jump directly to any lesson.
This is a scripted demonstration of the real Windows interface.
Transcript text, device names, and answers are samples.
No meeting, microphone, or remote model is used.
Click guides show scripted control activations.
Native file pickers are omitted;
sample files and clipboard output stay isolated.
The current source includes the Previous answer toggle.
The published version zero point two preview one does not include that newer feature.
This tutorial does not update the published installer, and it does not prove that every screen-sharing
product excludes the window.
On the private GitHub release page, download the Windows eleven, sixty-four-bit Setup
file. Check the published checksum.
Open Setup, review the unsigned-preview warning, and follow the installer.
Finish and close Setup, then launch Phantom Fudge from Start.
Setup does not launch it for you.
The installer is per-user.
It bundles the desktop runtime, local speech runtime, and speech models.
You do not need developer tools, system Python, or Docker for normal installed use.
Answer providers are separate: installing Phantom Fudge does not configure an AI account.
For the portable package, extract the entire archive and open Phantom Fudge dot Launcher in
its launcher folder. Keep the whole extraction together.
For the latest source, follow the prerequisites and use the repository launcher.
That source route includes the newer previous-answer feature.
Source development uses PowerShell seven point two or later, Python three point thirteen,
and the .NET ten SDK selected by global dot JSON.
Follow the Desktop Runtime prerequisite for development builds.
Initialize Transcription prepares dependencies and models before the source launcher runs.
Installed normal use does not require these developer tools.
If speech startup fails, the installed launcher offers Open notes without transcription.
The source equivalent is Notes Only.
This skips speech-service startup;
it does not disable an already configured answer provider or stop an existing service.
Before an update, save notes, export anything you need, and close the app with
X. Then run the newer versioned Setup.
The installer supports install, repair, and update;
an app that has not finished shutting down is not a successful update.
To remove the installed app, open Windows Settings, Apps, Installed apps,
then find Phantom Fudge and choose Uninstall.
External notes, exports, and settings are retained.
Uninstalling the program is not a secure erase of those separate files.
The app starts in presentation mode, with notes collapsed.
The transcript is on the left; your question and answer are on the right.
Both audio sources are selected by default, but nothing is recorded until you explicitly press
Start.
Click Hide Q slash A to collapse the question pane.
It also cancels an active answer and stops provider preparation.
Your transcript and saved files are not erased.
Click Show Q slash A to bring the question workspace back.
Wide windows use side-by-side panes;
narrower windows adapt the layout.
Drag the empty title-bar grip to move the window, not the text area.
Drag an edge or corner to resize it.
Keep the controls comfortably readable.
There is no ordinary taskbar button;
use the recovery shortcut or relaunch the app if you lose the window.
Here the window is narrowed.
The actual interface rearranges itself instead of placing every control in a scrolling outer panel.
Long text can still scroll inside its own reader.
Use a wider window when you want the transcript and answer visible together.
A wider layout is helpful for the first walkthrough.
Click the sun and theme-name button to switch to Harbor Daylight.
The next theme is named on the button;
your transcript and question are preserved.
Click Plain B slash W for the neutral black-and-white look.
It is a theme reset, not a data reset.
Click the theme button again to return to Deep Sea Foam.
Choose whichever theme gives you the clearest reading contrast.
Drag Background toward ten percent to make the background more transparent.
The text stays solid.
This is not click-through, and it does not make the process hidden.
Drag Background back toward one hundred percent when the material behind the window makes text difficult
to read. This setting is for the current session.
Click Audio setup.
Opening it closes Q slash A and cancels its answer or preparation, but does not stop
audio. Stop before changing devices.
These cards use sample names;
on your machine they show the available Windows devices.
Click Computer to transcribe the sound played by your selected output device.
This can include other applications and microphone sidetone, not just the meeting.
Click the card for the device where you actually hear the meeting, such as your headphones.
The highlighted border and filled dot identify the selection.
Click Mic if you only want microphone transcription.
This is a separate source; the app does not read meeting chat messages.
Choose the microphone you intend to use.
If that selected input fails during capture, the session stops rather than silently substituting
another microphone. After an explicit Refresh, check the selected card again.
Click Both to use Computer and Mic together.
Their transcript lines keep separate source labels.
Those labels identify the input track, not individual people in the meeting.
While stopped, click Refresh after connecting hardware.
Either Refresh button rediscovers both device lists.
The previous selection stays if its device still exists;
otherwise the first available device is selected.
Recheck both cards before Start.
For a machine with many outputs, the card layout adds page arrows.
This sample list shows that behavior without changing any Windows audio settings.
Click the right arrow to see the next page.
The page label also tells you which page contains the currently selected device.
Click the left arrow to go back.
Changing pages does not itself select a different device.
We will return to the small sample device list.
In normal use, select your intended card before leaving setup.
Click Service setup to see the session-only local service token field.
Normally the launcher supplies this for you.
Edit mode enables manual entry;
never publish or paste your actual token into a tutorial or chat.
Click Close service setup to put the advanced field away.
Native local recognition is the normal path;
Docker is not a startup requirement.
Click Done to return to the workspace.
Choosing devices and closing setup do not begin transcription.
Click Start. In normal use this starts the selected audio inputs.
Here it starts only the labelled sample stream.
The red dot means selected inputs are running, not merely selected.
A partial line appears while recognition is still in progress.
It can change as more speech arrives.
Treat it as provisional, especially before sending it as a question.
The completed line moves into the transcript history with its Computer label.
Local recognition is fallible, so review important words and names.
A microphone line is labelled Mic.
Computer and Mic stay separate even when Both is selected.
Headphones help reduce speaker echo that a microphone might pick up.
New lines continue arriving while you read.
The app does not automatically send the entire meeting to an answer provider.
You choose the text to ask about.
Click Stop to stop the selected audio inputs.
Wait for final draining and the stopped state before changing devices.
Stop does not cancel a separate answer, and an accepted final transcript line may still
arrive while draining. This workflow does not save raw audio.
Click the first transcript line.
Its text becomes a local question draft, and question editing opens.
A click does not send anything.
Click the microphone line as well.
Multiple lines combine in transcript order, not in the order you happened to click them.
Click the selected microphone line again to remove it.
You can build a useful question without copying unrelated meeting context.
Select the microphone line again because it contains the useful instruction to keep the answer concise.
Review the assembled draft before editing.
Edit the draft into the exact question you want answered.
Typing here is independent of Notes Edit and does not stop transcription.
If you now click another transcript line, the app keeps your edited draft instead of silently
overwriting it. Clear the question first when you truly want a new selection.
Click Done to leave question editing.
This is not Ask; the reviewed text remains local.
Click Copy draft if you want to use the question somewhere else.
In real use this writes to the Windows clipboard, outside capture protection.
This demonstration uses an isolated clipboard sink.
Click Setup slash details.
Snapshot only is the safe local mode: it freezes your question without sending a model request.
Click Freeze locally. The submitted snapshot is a separate copy.
Later draft changes cannot rewrite that earlier snapshot.
Freezing returns to the reading view automatically.
You can reopen Setup slash details to inspect the provider notice and draft provenance.
The snapshot and draft remain separate.
Click Clear question, immediately to the right of Ask.
It clears the draft, snapshot, answer, clarification, and previous-answer selection.
It does not erase the meeting transcript or your notes.
Click Choose source for the compact selection panel.
This is an alternative to clicking the main transcript directly.
Click Mic to show microphone segments in this chooser.
Filtering changes what you browse;
it does not send a question.
Click the microphone segment you want.
Then use the explicit Use selected action to copy that selection into your draft.
Click Use selected. The app creates the draft locally;
Ask remains a separate action.
Open Choose source again and use All to browse both tracks.
Computer filters to playback only.
The source chooser is optional; direct transcript clicks are usually faster.
Close the chooser and clear this sample question so we can move on to the answer workflow.
Phantom Fudge supports an installed Agency provider, direct Copilot, or a separately configured
local model. Agency and ordinary Copilot can use remote model services.
A local command-line process does not by itself mean offline inference.
In the source workflow, use Initialize Answers with Provider Agency.
Use the exact qualified Agency build shown here;
other versions fail until qualified.
The helper writes non-secret settings and may build the app.
It does not install Agency or sign you in.
Then return and Reload setup.
Direct Copilot requires a separately installed compatible CLI, with the supported versions
shown here. Choose Provider Copilot through the source helper.
Connect explicitly starts sign-in;
do not trigger it casually during a meeting.
This hosted route remains unqualified after an earlier failed smoke attempt.
LocalModel needs both a compatible direct Copilot CLI and an already-running OpenAI-compatible
model server. Configure its real model identifier and loopback endpoint.
There is no hosted fallback, but a local endpoint could itself proxy remotely, so
verify the server's behavior.
No actual local model was qualified here.
This is a source-checkout example, not an installed model promise.
Replace the model and port with your real setup.
The helper writes this user's answers dot JSON at the shown path.
Installed packages omit the helper;
use the provider guide for that file's schema, then Reload setup.
Click Setup slash details to inspect the mode and provider notice.
This panel selects and reloads settings;
it is not an account, model, or executable-path editor.
Read the data boundary before enabling a provider.
After changing provider configuration, click Reload setup.
Loading configuration does not submit your question.
The real Agency path may prepare its transport in the background.
For the remaining lessons, this isolated copy uses a sample provider instead of contacting
Agency. The application still runs its real question, streaming,
context, and clarification state changes.
Click Snapshot only whenever you want to freeze questions without sending them.
Changing provider mode resets previous-answer context and clarification.
Click the configured-provider button to enable answers again.
On a real Agency setup, wait for readiness;
if preparation fails, read the status rather than repeatedly pressing Ask.
Close Setup slash details.
The question reader is now ready for an explicit request.
Click Type slash edit to enter a question directly.
You do not need a transcript selection if you already know what to ask.
Type a clear question with the constraints you want.
Only this reviewed question is used, unless you explicitly enable a documented context
option.
Click Ask provider. The app freezes the exact text and streams the answer into the reader.
This sample response is scripted, not evidence of model quality or latency.
Wait for the completed answer before relying on it.
The answer is plain text.
You remain responsible for checking accuracy and speaking in your own words.
Drag the Size slider in the answer section.
It changes the answer and interpretation font from eight to twenty-four, for this session only.
It does not resize the transcript or notes.
Click Copy answer to copy the displayed result.
The Windows clipboard is not protected by the window's capture policy.
This tutorial routes copying to an isolated sink.
While Agency is preparing, use Cancel preparation, or Cancel prep in a narrow layout.
Wait for cleanup. Use configured provider or Reload setup prepares it again.
Cancelling preparation does not stop transcription.
Preparation differs from a submitted answer;
neither guarantees a fixed response time.
For a follow-up, click Previous answer immediately to the left of Ask.
It is off by default.
Turning it on does not send anything;
the next explicit Ask captures the completed answer currently displayed.
Edit the question to your follow-up.
Do not click Clear first: Clear would remove the answer you want to use as context.
Click Ask provider. This request includes the new question and one immutable previous-answer
snapshot. It does not automatically include old questions, older answers,
notes, or the whole meeting.
Open Setup slash details after the response completes.
The previous-answer field shows the exact submitted context, not whatever happens to be displayed
later.
Close details. After a successful follow-up, the option stays on,
but the next request uses only the newest completed answer.
Failed, cancelled, and unfinished output is not eligible.
Click Previous answer again for an unrelated question.
It turns off without sending.
Clear and provider changes also reset this selection.
Click Clear question, then Done, to begin a separate example outside question-edit mode.
This deliberately discards the previous Q slash A state while keeping the transcript.
Check Clarify first.
The first request will ask for an interpretation rather than a solution.
Checking the box alone does not make a request.
Click Type slash edit and write the question that needs clarification.
Click Done when the wording is ready.
Click Interpret question.
The app locks the original draft and displays an interpretation.
This is not the final answer.
Read what the provider thinks you mean.
If it is correct, use Yes, answer.
If it is wrong or incomplete, type a correction instead.
Copy interpretation copies what the provider thinks you mean, not a confirmed solution.
Copy original preserves the original question rather than substituting the correction field.
Click Type reply to enable the reply editor.
A correction does not silently replace the original draft.
Specify what was missing.
Here we request a remote-audience example and three practical tips.
Yes, answer is disabled while a correction is written, so it cannot silently discard
that correction.
Click Send reply. This sends the correction with this question's clarification history.
The app waits for another interpretation;
it does not auto-confirm.
Once the revised interpretation is correct, click Yes, answer.
Typing exact Yes and pressing Send reply also confirms, ignoring surrounding whitespace
and case. Yes, but followed by more text is a correction, not confirmation.
The solution now appears.
Previous answer, when enabled initially, stays pinned through clarification.
After four interpretations, confirm the intended question or Clear to start over.
Setup slash details shows the extra instruction and completed clarification exchanges.
Uncheck Clarify first when you no longer need the interpretation step.
The original question remains available.
We will demonstrate a deliberately slow sample response.
There is no real model request or network delay in this example.
Click Ask provider. While a response is in progress, do not start another
request or switch providers.
Click Cancel answer and wait for cleanup.
Any copied partial result begins with Incomplete answer in square brackets.
It is not a completed answer and cannot become previous-answer context.
Click Clear question when you want to discard the cancelled result and begin again.
This does not clear your meeting transcript.
Read the provider status.
Check configuration and authorization through the provider's documented setup, then Reload setup.
Do not paste tokens into the question, and do not assume a failed local model will fall back
to the cloud. Snapshot only remains available for local question drafting.
Click Notes to expand the speaker-note area.
This closes Q slash A and cancels its answer or preparation, but leaves transcription
running and preserves the question.
Entering global Notes Edit next is different: that stops audio too.
Click the top-bar Edit button.
Unlike question editing, global Notes Edit stops transcription and cancels answer or preparation
activity. It enables note typing and file operations.
Control Alt E is the direct Notes Edit shortcut.
Type plain-text notes in the editor.
Keep prompts short enough to glance at.
New notes are not automatically saved.
With keyboard-control mode inactive, Notes Edit supports Control S, O,
N and F for save, open, new and find.
Control Z undoes recent note edits, with a hundred undo units.
New and a successful Open clear that history.
Undo is not autosave or recovery of a discarded document.
Click A plus to enlarge the notes text.
This control is separate from the answer Size slider.
Click A minus to reduce the notes font again.
The notes control supports sizes from twelve to forty-two.
Uncheck Wrap if you want long lines to remain on one line with horizontal scrolling.
This affects notes, not the answer reader.
Check Wrap again for a compact, glanceable note.
Content is preserved when wrapping changes.
Click Find to open the note search field.
This search is separate from transcript search in keyboard mode.
Type the word you want to find.
Here we will search for example.
Click Next to select the next match.
The search wraps back to the beginning when needed.
Click Close find when you are finished.
Your note is still unsaved until you explicitly save it.
Click Save. On the first save, choose a destination in the Windows file picker.
The picker is omitted here; the real save operation writes only an isolated sample file.
Saved locally confirms the write.
Use Save as when you want another destination or need to resolve a file that changed outside the app.
Do not overwrite a file without checking what it contains.
Click Open and choose a UTF-eight text file.
This demo opens an isolated example.
The app accepts files up to one mebibyte and retains your current content if opening fails.
Make an edit to see the unsaved-change safeguard.
The status clearly says there are unsaved changes.
Click New. Because the note is unsaved, an inline confirmation appears.
Save notes, cancel, or explicitly discard;
do not treat closing the panel as a save.
Click Cancel to keep the unsaved note and return to editing.
Click New once more. We will deliberately discard only this throwaway sample draft.
Click Discard and continue.
The new blank note appears.
This is a destructive choice for unsaved note text, not an undoable save.
Click Present when you are ready to read rather than edit.
The note becomes read-only.
Audio does not automatically restart.
Click Notes to collapse the area.
Collapsing is just a layout action, not a save or delete.
Click Edit before exporting.
Export is intentionally disabled in presentation mode because native file dialogs are outside
capture assurance.
Click Export and choose a text-file destination.
The Windows picker is omitted in this demo.
The transcript is saved as text;
no audio recording is written.
Open Audio setup after export.
Clear transcript is inside this panel, separate from the red Clear question button.
Click Clear transcript after recording has stopped and the transcript has been exported.
If it is still unsaved, the app refuses to clear it and asks you to export first.
Click Done, then Present to leave file-edit mode.
Nothing resumes recording automatically.
Collapse Notes and show Q slash A again.
We will load a fresh sample conversation for keyboard practice.
The next lines are synthetic practice text.
Keyboard controls let you select, review, and submit without moving a mouse around the window.
Click Keys, or press Control Alt K.
The strip says Control.
Letters act as commands only in this local mode;
there is no global letter hook.
From Control, I enters question or reply editing directly.
Press F1, or question mark, for the on-screen key map.
Escape returns to Control.
Press Escape. The mode label returns to Control;
you have not submitted a question.
Press V to enter Select mode.
Use J and K, or the arrow keys, to move between transcript rows.
Moving the cursor does not select a row.
Press G twice to jump to the first available row.
Shift G jumps to the latest row.
Page keys move through larger lists.
Press Space to select the highlighted row.
Pressing it again deselects that row.
Press J to move down, then Space to add the second row.
The draft combines selected text locally.
Press one to browse Mic rows.
Two shows Computer, and three restores all sources.
Existing selected rows are preserved when you filter.
Press three to see all sources again.
Press F3, or slash, to open transcript search.
This is not the note Find feature, and it does not call a model.
Type remote, then press Enter to find matching transcript text.
To clear the filter later, open Search, erase its text, and press Enter.
Escape from Search returns to Select.
Press Enter from Select mode to move into Edit.
That Enter only prepares the draft for review.
Control Enter cannot bypass this review while you are still selecting.
In Edit mode, letters are normal text and Enter adds a newline.
Control Enter explicitly submits.
Escape to Control before using modal F one help or F two commands.
Press Control Enter to send the reviewed question.
This uses the same snapshot and provider rules as clicking Ask.
Wait for the answer, then press Escape to return to Control.
Leaving Edit does not make another request.
Press A to enter Read mode.
J and K, arrows, and page keys move through the answer;
Home and End reach its boundaries.
Press plus to enlarge the answer.
Minus reduces it, within the same eight-to-twenty-four range as the slider.
Press End to move to the end, then Home to return to the beginning.
The text itself is unchanged.
Press Escape to return to Control before choosing another mode.
Press F2 to open the built-in command line.
Type font sixteen for an exact answer size.
Press Enter to execute this command.
Read the status before moving on.
Press F2 to open the built-in command line.
Type context on to include the displayed completed answer on your next explicit Ask.
Press Enter to execute this command.
Read the status before moving on.
Press F2 to open the built-in command line.
Type context off for an unrelated question.
Press Enter to execute this command.
Read the status before moving on.
Press F2 to open the built-in command line.
Type devices to open keyboard device selection.
First stop transcription and finish or cancel any answer.
Press Enter to execute this command.
Read the status before moving on.
In Devices mode, arrow keys move the highlighted card.
Space selects it. Tab switches between Computer and Mic;
left and right brackets change pages when more devices exist.
Press Escape to close device setup and return to Control.
Press F2 to open the built-in command line.
Type theme light to switch the visual theme without using the pointer.
Press Enter to execute this command.
Read the status before moving on.
Press F2 to open the built-in command line.
Type opacity eighty-five to set background tint directly.
Press Enter to execute this command.
Read the status before moving on.
Press F2 to open the built-in command line.
Type theme dark to return to Deep Sea Foam.
Press Enter to execute this command.
Read the status before moving on.
Press F2 and type font.
Tab can complete a matching built-in command;
Escape cancels without executing it.
Press Escape to leave this completed suggestion without running it.
Commands also cover start, stop, source Mic or Computer or Both, clarify
on or off, confirm, copy question, copy answer, clear question,
cancel, ask, mask, and help.
Each command uses the same guarded action as the corresponding interface control.
This is not a shell.
Save the exact three-field UTF-eight JSON shown here as keyboard dot JSON,
then restart after saving work.
Control Alt stays fixed.
Enabled false disables global activation, not Keys.
Invalid settings or a shortcut conflict leave Keys available.
Use your configured activation key rather than assuming K.
Press Escape from Control to leave keyboard mode.
Returning focus to the earlier application is best-effort.
Switching applications disarms the controller.
Use Keys or your configured Control Alt activation chord to enter again.
Click the book icon at the top left.
The workspace is replaced by Notepad is ready, with the same icon available to restore it.
The cover changes what the window displays.
Transcription and answers can continue underneath it.
It does not provide universal invisibility, erase data, or hide the process from Windows.
Click the book icon again to restore the workspace.
The current question, answer, and layout return.
Enter keyboard control with Control Alt K, then press M.
Masking disarms keyboard mode and shows the cover.
Press Control Alt K again to restore the workspace and enter Control mode.
This is useful when you do not want to reach for the pointer.
Press Escape to leave keyboard control before the next pointer action.
Click Hide. Unlike Cover, it hides the window, stops transcription, and
cancels answer or preparation activity.
The blank stage shows the hidden window.
Reveal it when ready, then start transcription again explicitly.
Press Control Alt Space to reveal the window again.
Relaunching the app is another recovery route.
Hiding and recovery do not automatically resume recording.
Click Diagnostics to reload diagnostic settings and open the local log folder outside window protection.
Default logs contain timing and error metadata, not audio or text bodies.
Text logging is a separate retention choice.
Run these diagnostic helpers from the source checkout.
Installed packages omit them.
After changing the mode, click Diagnostics or restart to apply it.
Export stays local and excludes text unless Include Text is requested.
Clearing the interface does not erase old logs or provider retention.
Confirm the meeting plays through the selected Computer device, and that Mic is enabled only when intended.
Check Windows microphone permission if needed.
Stop before refreshing devices.
If the service or token is missing, use the documented launcher and local service setup;
do not paste a secret into notes.
Before relying on capture exclusion, test your exact sharing mode with a recipient and harmless
text. A successful Windows protection request is not proof of what an audience sees.
Native dialogs, files, clipboard history, accessibility, cameras, and unsupported
capture paths remain separate boundaries.
Click Details in the status area to read the capture limitation in the application.
Keep this distinction in mind even when the window looks quiet.
Click Details again to return to the compact status.
Click X to exit. If notes, transcript, or question text remain unsaved,
the inline confirmation gives you a chance to preserve them.
Copy question text before discarding;
a note save is not a transcript export.
Click Cancel to keep the app and current content.
The exit attempt already stopped transcription and provider work before this confirmation.
Cancel does not resume them.
Save, export or copy what you need, then restart transcription explicitly if continuing.
For a normal session: check your sharing path, choose the correct devices, press
Start, select and review the question, then explicitly Ask.
Use Previous answer for a follow-up, and Clarify first when wording is unclear.
At the end, Stop, save or export what you need, and exit.
You have now seen the interface, optional provider setup, transcript and notes workflows,
follow-up context, clarification, keyboard modes, and recovery.
The chapter player and searchable transcript let you revisit any step without watching the whole tutorial
again.
